newsitem.title: USA: Morrison Knudsen profits rise after merger.
newsitem.headline: Morrison Knudsen profits rise after merger.

text.p: Morrison Knudsen Corp. Friday, marking the first quarter after its merger with Washington Construction Group, Inc., reported sharply higher profits in the fourth quarter.

Morrison Knudsen posted net income of $5.6 million, or 11 cents per share, for the fourth quarter ended Nov. 30, almost double the $2.9 million, or 10 cents per share, in the year-ago period. Revenue surged to $416.7 million from $68.3 million.

The results combine those of Washington Construction from Dec. 1, 1995 to Nov. 30, 1996 and of Morrison Knudsen from Sept. 12, 1996 to Nov. 30, 1996. On Sept. 11, the companies merged to form Morrison Knudsen Corp.
Operating income rose to $9.8 million from $3.2 million in the 1995 fourth quarter, it said.

"We ended the year in a strong financial position and with our recent major new work bookings, we are well positioned for the future," said Robert Tinstman, chief executive officer of the Boise, Idaho-based company.
Tinstman said Morrison Knudsen ended its fiscal year debt free and with a net worth of more than $300 million and a $200 million line of credit.
Backlog of uncompleted contracts as of Nov. 30, was $3.5 billion, he said.

In addition to $200 million in new work booked in the fourth quarter, major new contracts in the first month of the new fiscal year include two awards anticipated to provide about $500 million in revenue, he said.
Morrison Knudsen's stock was unchanged at $9.625 on the New York Stock Exchange in late trading.
